findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body: When callers invoke the returned teardown while the socket remains active, the registered `message` handler stays attached. Repeated attach/teardown cycles retain captured state and invoke stale or duplicate handlers on later messages. Restore `socket.off("message", handler)` in the callback.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
After `attach()` returns, invoking its disposer no longer unregisters the `"message"` listener. Any subsequent message still invokes the handler, and repeated attach/dispose cycles retain listeners, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned teardown
findings.body:
Any caller invoking the returned cleanup while the socket remains active will continue receiving `"message"` events. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate handlers, causing duplicate processing and memory leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer revokes message delivery. If a shared socket remains open after a session/component is torn down, a peer can send another message and invoke a stale handler that the caller believes was detached, potentially processing data under an expired authorization or lifecycle context.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned disposer
findings.body:
On any long-lived socket, calling the returned cleanup function no longer unregisters the handler. Repeated attach/dispose cycles retain handlers, leak their captured memory, and multiply per-message work and callbacks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
